decisions.reason: IEA Trends in electric cars, notes under electric car sales: BEV and plug-in hybrid are included; ordinary HEV is excluded.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Japan paragraph reports conventional HEV separately from electric car sales.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Electric car sales opening reports more than 20 million worldwide in 2025; retain lower-bound wording.
IEA Trends in electric cars, China paragraph reports more than 13 million electric cars sold in 2025; BEV plus PHEV.
IEA Trends in electric cars, China paragraph says almost 55% of new car sales in 2025; retain approximate wording.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Japan paragraph says 2025 electric car sales were just above 100,000; retain lower-bound wording.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Japan paragraph says electric cars accounted for less than 3% of car sales in 2025.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Japan paragraph gives conventional HEVs around one-third of all 2025 car sales; HEV is not BEV or PHEV.
IEA Trends in electric cars, China paragraph estimates 44 million electric cars on Chinese roads at end-2025; this is stock, not annual sales.
IEA Trends in electric cars, China paragraph says 2025 electric car sales growth was less than 20% year on year.
IEA Manufacturing and trade chapter reports China produced 16 million electric cars in 2025; production differs from domestic sales.
IEA Manufacturing and trade chapter reports more than 2.5 million Chinese electric car exports in 2025; shipments differ from overseas sales.
IEA Manufacturing and trade chapter reports China over 80% of 2025 battery cell production; this is output, not car sales.
China State Council portal, 14 January 2026, cites CAAM sales of 16.49 million NEVs in 2025. Keep NEV separate from IEA electric-car metric and paraphrase without copying page content.
IEA Cutting through the noise, page 1, identifies large manufacturing scale and fixed-cost spreading as a cost advantage; it is not a model-by-model comparison.
IEA Cutting through the noise, page 1, says lower battery costs make the electric-car production cost advantage greater than for ICE cars; not retail price.
IEA Cutting through the noise, page 1, links widespread LFP adoption to avoiding costlier nickel-based materials; do not generalize to every car.
IEA Cutting through the noise, page 1, attributes early scale partly to subsidies and preferential financing and says policy alone does not explain prices.
IEA Cutting through the noise, page 1, says manufacturing efficiency accounts for over 40% of the China-Europe battery production cost gap; not China-Japan.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Japan paragraph links high HEV share with automakers' long-standing hybrid focus for fuel economy; attribution is IEA analysis.
IEA Trends in electric cars, Japan paragraph identifies limited private parking in apartments and charging constraints as factors slowing sales; no effect size given.
JAMA 2025 passenger-car survey, purchase intentions section, gives 46% for next intended car across HEV, PHEV, BEV and FCEV. Survey intent is not sales; paraphrase only.
JAMA 2025 passenger-car survey, environmental-car attitudes section, places HEV highest for first purchase-consideration rank; survey result only.
JAMA 2025 passenger-car survey, environmental-car attitudes section, says respondents reported more concerns for BEV than other types; no national causal claim.
JAMA 2025 passenger-car survey, environmental-car attitudes section, says detached-house BEV/PHEV users mostly installed and use home charging; limited to surveyed group.
